The simulated experimental results show that the output power ratio changing is in a good agreement at the design frequency.

articleTitle: LED alert bracelet for patients with cognitive dysfunction
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: In this study, an energy-efficient, configurable chip that can store and display phone numbers was designed. The chip is incorporated into an alert bracelet that can be used by people with cognitive dysfunction. The bracelet provides an uncomplicated, flexible, operationally safe, and cost-effective method for locating wandering and disoriented people.

articleTitle: Microwave breast imaging using a non-conventional magnitude-combined approach
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: A non-conventional Magnitude-Combined microwave imaging method is proposed for breast cancer detection. The optimal frequency band is selected for a maximum selectivity to malignancy.

articleTitle: Design of the broadband balun with modified impedance transformer and phase inverter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: The planar balun with a broad operating band is presented. This balun is composed of a wideband power divider and one 180° phase inverter. In order to obtain a broad operating band, the modified impedance transformer with three stages is adopted. Well-matched results of simulation and measurement can validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable output power 4×4 Butler matrix
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: A reconfigurable output power 4×4 Butler matrix consisted of four adjustable output power ratio branch line couplers and two 45 degree phase shifters is proposed. The adjustable output power ratio branch line coupler is accomplished by simply changing the values of two shunted capacitors. The simulated antenna factors of four different inputs changes as predication are also presented.

articleTitle: Event localization of RF devices used in elderly care
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This paper discusses the problem of detecting wearable RF devices used in elderly care. Events such as blood sugar level drop, or physical fall of the elderly person, are stochastic events and are digitally recorded and/or broadcast to a monitoring system through home. The stochastic nature of the events and independence of the digital broadcast for different events are exploited here to allow localization of the RF devices upon occurrences of events using multiple signal classification approach for stochastically-active source localization.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties and water contents of biological tissue after microwave heating
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: In this study, the relationship between the water content ratio [wt%] and the dielectric properties of the dehydrated liver tissues were measured. Employing the results of this study, the numerical dielectric model of dehydrated liver tissue will be developed for the numerical analysis of microwave coagulation therapy (MCT) for liver cancer. Small pieces of swine liver tissue were heated and dehydrated in the household microwave oven to make measurement samples with low water content ratios. The dielectric constants (relative permittivity and conductivity [S/m]) of samples at 2.45 GHz were measured by the open-ended coaxial probe technique. After the measurement of dielectric constants, water content ratios of samples were measured by the loss on drying (LOD) technique. As a result, the relative permittivity and the conductivity of samples strongly depended on water content ratios of them.

articleTitle: A fast volume integral equation solver for electromagnetic simulation with complex voxel based magnetodielectric human model in MRI applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This work presents a fast volume integral equation solver named the mixed order BCGS-FFT method for electromagnetic simulations of high resolution human bodies with both dielectric and magnetic susceptibility contrasts in MRI application. The mixed order BCGS-FFT method is an accurate and efficient solver developed for magnetodielectric objects. A numerical calculation of the electromagnetic responses of a high resolution voxel human head model shows a high efficiency of the mixed order BCGS-FFT method in both computational complexity and memory requirement.

articleTitle: Simulation of 2-D coherent imaging based on regular antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: We introduce a novel microwave imaging system based on compressed sensing(CS), allowing image reconstruction with fewer samples than conventional required. It is found that a sparse scene could be rebuilt under acceptable non-correlated condition. The illumination patterns of regular antennas are non-correlation enough for compressive sensing through frequency diversity. As simulation demonstrated, a sparse target is rebuilt in a 2D scene by leveraging of CS with a pair of non-special designed horn antennas and a receiving dipole.

articleTitle: Electroporation control of complex cell system by varying pulse voltage and duration
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: Electroporation is a common but efficient method for cell therapy. Pulses of duration ranging from microsecond to nanosecond with specific voltage have been studied in recent 20 years. Since electric field is also an important factor for effects on cell pore formation, we apply 100 ns and 10 ns pulses by varying their voltage acting on the complex cell system. Prediction of electroporation effects is obtained and guidance can be offered for experiments. Furthermore, a special short duration pulse may be designed to cause organelle tp electroporate.

articleTitle: Ground plane effects on SAR for human head model exposed to a dual-band PIFA
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: Effects of ground plane on the Specific absorption rate (SAR) in SAM head model exposed PIFA antenna is investigated in this paper. The dual-band PIFA working at 900M and 1800M is designed to operate with a ground plane, and the ground plane is an integral part of the antenna assembly. To investigate systematic biases on SAR in SAM head model resulting from shape effect of the ground, both the average SAR over a mass of 1g and 10g in the head models exposed to a dual band PIFA were determined. These results are very useful in the design of a PIFA for applications requiring a small ground plane.

articleTitle: Microwave medical imaging at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: We introduce a novel Ka-band microwave imaging system operating at 35 GHz. Central to the performance of this system is a direct field inversion algorithm requiring only one minute of processing time per image slice cross section. The imaging system is a single-frequency transmission device, consisting of a stationary single Ka-band transmit horn antenna and a Ka-band open-ended waveguide receive probe equipped with a position-scanning mechanism. Once these single-slice, single-frequency test data are captured, a 3D image of tissue structure is obtained through our Field Mapping Algorithm (FMA), which uses the two tangential electric field components on the exterior surface, be it a plane, a sphere, or a cylinder, to determine the field throughout the tissue interior. The tissue medium associated with the interior field distribution is thus revealed as to its structure by way of the field polarization attributes. Two test measurement results are presented, one for a biological, and one for an inanimate dielectric object. Good imaging is clearly evident in these two measurement cases, despite the significant and unavoidable microwave absorption in the millimeter range.

articleTitle: Plasmonic enhanced optical disk reactor for wastewater treatment
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: A process of growing large-area plasmonic-nano-particles-decorated ZnO nanorods on the polycarbonate optical disk substrate was developed, while a corresponding photocatalytic rotational reactor was fabricated. Hydrothermal process was adapted to grow ZnO nanorods perpendicular to the optical disk substrate at relatively lower temperature. The optical disk substrate has advantages of durable property in fast rotation and high impact-resistance. The plasmonic nano-particles, in this case, silver nano-particles, were deposed on the ZnO nanorods by direct sputtering. The morphology of ZnO nanorods and plasmonic nano-particles was investigated by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). The photocatalytic activity of the sample was evaluated by the degradation of methyl orange (MO) as a model compound in aqueous solution, and the decomposition rate of MO molecules is monitored by the optical spectroscopy measurements. In the optimized condition, less than 10% of the MO remained in the aqueous solution after a 20-minute treatment in the rotational reactor with our sample.

articleTitle: Assessment of dielectric properties for the microwave phantom production
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This research presents an assessment of dielectric properties for the microwave phantom production (MPP). The presented MPP was constructed by mixing organic compounds and inorganic compounds, which having particular dielectric properties. In addition, the fabricated MPP was analyzed to evaluate the relative electromagnetic properties based on the basic concepts of microstrip lines. Moreover, the characteristic parameter of the MPP, such as dielectric constant, was extracted effectively by converting the relative electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: Electron density determination for plasma assisted sterilization processes
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: An effective measurement concept for the precise determination of the electron density in plasma assisted sterilization processes is presented in this paper. Here, plasmas offer a promising approach for heat or chemical sensitive materials, like surgery instruments. Therefore, the Multipole Resonance Probe (MRP) is investigated over a wide frequency range. Based on the evaluation of an unambiguous resonance behaviour, the resonance frequency can be determined from 0.5 to 6 GHz. Proven in 3D electromagnetic field simulations and measurements in an excited Argon plasma, the additional center of gravity method increases the performance and the MRP can be used for an evaluation of a wide density range. Hence, the density can be controlled effectively and used in a feedback control loop.

articleTitle: A novel body-worn RF sensor for deep tissue imaging
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: We present a novel body-worn sensor for continuous real-time imaging of deep human tissues. The sensor operates at 40 MHz, and consists of a set of transmitting and receiving probes placed around the human body. Preliminary results show that the sensor can provide 16-pixel images of the underlying cross-section with accuracy better than 5%. Remarkably, this is the first time that tissues deep into the body can be imaged pixel-by-pixel using a portable body-worn approach. Overall, the proposed sensor brings forward a new approach for real-time deep-tissue monitoring to be used in a wide range of applications (e.g., prevention of cardiovascular diseases, tumor growth monitoring, etc.).

articleTitle: Plaster type wearable dual band planar antenna with double loop made of fabric cloth for BAN
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This paper describes the simulated results of wearable plaster type dual band antenna with double loop made of fabric cloth for BAN. Wide bandwidth of VSWR less than 2 at ISM band (2.4-2.5 GHz) and UWB band (7.25-10.25 GHz) was obtained when the proposed antenna was mounted on finger. The influence of next finger was made clear.

articleTitle: Vertical split-ring resonators based plasmon coupling, nanophotonic sensing and light manipulation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: We present vertical split-ring resonators (VSRRs) which behave as magnetic metamolecules sensitive to both the incident electric and magnetic fields upon excitation. A couple of potential applications such as VSRR-based highly sensitive refractive-index sensor and metasurface for light manipulation in optical communication frequency will also be demonstrated.

articleTitle: A standing-wave enevelope detection tecnique for breath and heartbeat rates detection (invited)
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: A standing-wave envelope detection technique is applied to detect breath and heart-beat rates. The breath and heart-beat periodic motions modulate the envelope of received RF standing-wave waveform in addition to the well-known Doppler phase modulation of the RF carrier. Therefore, a new vital signal radar is developed for detecting the breath and heart-beat rates and compared with the conventional Doppler radar.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit approach to improve the isolation of the diversity antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: Utilization of the equivalent circuit model has shown more time-effective for designing RF circuits and antennas rather than Electromagnetic fields analysis. This study investigates equivalent circuit perspective on designing the resonant antenna. An equivalent π-network circuit is firstly proposed to approach the electromagnetic fields coupling of a closely coupled two-element diversity antenna. Thus, the improvement on the isolation between antennae can be straightforward achieved by employing resonant method. Numerical and experimental study are presented herein.

articleTitle: Design of the unequal power-divided dual-band coupler with coupled-line ring
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: The microstrip dual-band coupler with coupled-line ring has been provided. Within the proposed couplers, a coupled line with a half/quarter wavelength and two quarter-wavelength Schiffman phase shifters are adopted. The proposed couplers can not only be operated at two flexible frequencies with both 90° phase differences, but also provides the required output power ratio at the designed dual frequencies by the derived formulae. In order to verify the proposed design methodology, two experimental dual-band couplers are designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: Spectra implementation of medical diagnostic X-radiation standards beams
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: Available well-defined radiation conditions that can meet international standards are essential for medical device testing environment. The establishment of x-ray beam quality in radiology was recommended by IEC 61267. We have measured the half value layer (HVL) of RQR and RQA series beam qualities for use dictated by IEC standard. The ripple of the x-ray output and uncertainty were less than 10% and 1.5%. The half-value layer and homogeneity coefficient measurement differences between INER and IEC 61267 standard were also less than 5%. Also, it was noted that x-ray spectrum produced by XCOMP5 program and empirical methods could be used to calculate HVL and average energy. The compliance with IEC 61267 standard in radiology have been established and these standards provided radiation dose calibration, testing and dose traceability.

articleTitle: UWB microwave imaging for breast tumor detection based on shrinkage covariance matrix estimation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This paper presents a new covariance matrix estimate based on shrinkage method for breast tumor detection application. The parameters of shrinkage covariance matrix are obtained by solving a modified semi-definite programming (SDP) convex problem based on the mean-squared error (MSE) criterion. The reconstructed covariance matrix, using the determined shrinkage parameters, is then used to replace the conventional sample covariance matrix (SCM) in the beamformer. The performance of the resulting beamformer is tested by a 2-D numerical breast analysis model and the simulations show the proposed approach possesses a better target identification capability and improves the signal-to-clutter-noise ratio (SCNR).

articleTitle: Near-field antennas design with crossed-field elements to enhance the EM field strengths in the near zone
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of antenna design to radiate strong reactive fields in the vicinity of antenna. This antenna will compose the electric and magnetic fields in a manner similar their relationships in the far zone, and retains good radiation efficiency. Theoretic examination is first performed. Both numerical and experiment results will be presented in comparison with standard dipole and monopole antennas to justify the validity.

articleTitle: A current-mode PWM control CMOS power converter with novel slope compensation circuits for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: A lower power consumption, smaller output ripple and better regulation current-mode CMOS buck power converter with a novel on-chip slope compensation circuits for feedback control is presented in this paper. In current-mode converters, the slope compensation circuits needs to add ramp voltage signal with the inductor current signal in order to avoid subharmonic oscillation. The converter is designed and simulated using the TSMC 0.18um CMOS Process. Hspice simulation results show that, the buck converter having 1.129×1.200mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip size with power efficiency about 90%. This chip can operate with input supply voltage from 2.8V to 3.3V, and its output voltage can stable at 1.2V and less than 22mV ripple voltage at maximum loading current 500mA for biomedical or low power applications.

articleTitle: Design of lower limber movement information detection device
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: Under the advancement of medical technology and facing an aging society, the elderly still faces the problem of regular outpatient visits for their joint degeneration. It is a burden to the elderly. This study proposed a portable device based on internet concept, which is similar to a kneecap, and can continuously detect the joint condition and update the data to the cloud. The doctors can use the data stored in network database to assess the change conditions of patient's long-term personal physiological parameters, thus reducing the cost required for same examinations due to repeated incidence of disease. The patients may reduce the cost of outpatient visits.

articleTitle: Evaluation method for modulation transfer function determination of digital image detector
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: This study aimed to establish technology methods to evaluate MTF (modulation transfer function) for digital image system recommended by IEC 62220-1 and the use of a slit. The results showed that the difference was small between the knife edge and slit methods in the image analysis. However, the knife-edge method based on the slit technology is simple, easy to operate, and widely used. This method is used as a fundamental of the next research which calculates noise power spectrum (noise power spectra, NPS), and quantum efficiency (detective quantum efficiency, DQE).

articleTitle: Overview of vacuum electron devices for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE MTT-S 2015 International Microwave Workshop Series on RF and Wireless Technologies for Biomedical and Healthcare Applications (IMWS-BIO)
abstract: In this paper, we first introduce the high power vacuum electron devices (VEDs) such as magnetron, klystron, backward wave oscillator, traveling-wave tube, and gyrotron which can be used in the biomedical areas. And then we present the significant progress in the emerging metamaterial-inspired VEDs in our group in details and briefly address the future applications to the biomedical fields. Finally, in order to further improve the armarium's performance, we report the recent advances in the high power terahertz sources developed from the conventional VEDs and novel metamaterial VEDs.
